title: Linewise tables of word fragments
method:
A clerk sets one pair of outer-fragment cards beside each line, and draws the middle piece of each word fresh from a separate drawer. To prepare the tables, divide a word of length L into left and right pieces of floor(L/3) EVA-basic glyphs each and one centre containing the rest. Count joint outer pairs and centres separately, by length from 2 to 11, from certain words in the 192 public practice-training folios. A line draws its number of words and common glyph length from the training distributions for its kind. The book's public layout supplies the line kinds and paragraph-opening flags. Each outer card is drawn by its fitted frequency and is reused at every slot of its line. Middle cards are drawn independently with their fitted frequencies. The writer consults neither earlier spelling nor edit distance. Redraw the centre when a join would change the intended segmentation or create a prohibited four-word manuscript run. The fixed seed 408 specimen emits 5,225 lines and 38,753 tokens. The paired control shuffles the identical outer cards over all slots of the same glyph length, preserving their prevalence and line layouts. A within-line shuffle preserves the full word inventory of each line. Seed 409 is an unselected sensitivity specimen.

On the public practice split the fixed specimen has 647/4,826 qualifying edit-one events (0.134065), a page-shuffle mean of 0.011971 and p=0.005. The largest layout-matched reference rate is 0.017544. The actual manuscript has 134/4,379 (0.030601). Of the primary specimen's hits, 646 occur inside a line. Shuffling the outer pairs across slots lowers the rate to 0.015721. Shuffling words inside each line gives 0.135516. Seed 409 gives 0.146880. The procedure reproduces the thresholded diagnostic and substantially overshoots the manuscript's absolute rate.
